questions.q: Which core principle of democracy ensures that all adult citizens have the right to vote regardless of their caste, religion, wealth, or gender?
questions.a: Universal adult franchise. A student who answers "majoritarian rule" or "hereditary succession" misunderstands democracy as rule by a single group or family rather than political equality for every individual citizen.

questions.q: Why is government accountability considered one of the greatest advantages of a democratic system over a dictatorship?
questions.a: Because leaders in a democracy must face regular elections and answer to the public, forcing them to address citizens' needs and correct mistakes. A student who answers that democracy makes decisions faster misses the point; democracy values deliberation and accountability over speed, which prevents arbitrary tyranny.

questions.q: A village panchayat holds an open meeting (Gram Sabha) where citizens question the sarpanch about village funds spent on a new road. Which democratic principle is primarily at work here?
questions.a: Public accountability and transparency. A student who says "universal franchise" confuses voting in elections with ongoing citizen participation and oversight of elected officials during their term.

questions.q: How do fundamental rights (such as freedom of speech and expression) strengthen the advantages of a democratic government?
questions.a: Rights allow citizens to peacefully critique government policies, share diverse viewpoints, and hold leaders responsible without fear of punishment. A student who thinks rights only apply during election day fails to see that continuous free expression is essential for healthy democratic governance year-round.

questions.q: Evaluate this statement: "Democracy is inefficient because it requires endless debates and discussions among representatives." Is this a fair criticism, and why or why not?
questions.a: It is partially true that decision-making takes longer, but this inefficiency is actually a deliberate safeguard against hasty, unjust, or poorly thought-out laws. A student who completely agrees ignores that taking time to build consensus prevents social conflict and respects minority opinions, which authoritarian systems ignore at great human cost.

questions.q: Design a short civic charter for a school club that incorporates two key democratic principles: accountability and protection of minority views.
questions.a: A strong answer will establish a rule where club leaders must report spending monthly to all members (accountability) and decisions affecting small groups require special consensus or consultation so majority voting does not crush minority interests. A poor answer gives total, unchecked power to the club president.
